title: May I Ask for One Final Thing?
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Duke's daughter Scarlet is publicly dumped and framed as a 'villainess' by the second prince Kyle at a ball. Her 'one final request' is to punch him, and she goes on to beat up a faction of corrupt nobles who run slave auctions, while a cult of the love goddess Palmia targets her (Wikipedia; ANN; Alpha Manga blurb via AniList).
life_message: No one should have to swallow abuse, and the powerful who exploit others deserve to be stopped, with fists if need be.

content.note: Scarlet's beatings are the core appeal, 'violently cathartic' and comedic rather than gory (ANN; AV Club; MU Violent Female Lead).
Assassins and a cult, played mostly for action-comedy (Wikipedia; ANN).
Slow romance with Prince Julius; MangaDex rates it safe.
Years of abuse by her fiance are backstory (Alpha Manga blurb; MU Abusive Ex-Boyfriend).
Punching as the answer to mistreatment is celebrated (ANN; AV Club); worth discussing with younger readers.

dominant: Revenge on abusive elites; anti-slavery; a woman who refuses to stay quiet

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Public insult at the ball is answered with a punch, then a campaign of beatings (Wikipedia; ANN).

Order vs freedom.evidence: She acts outside rules but alongside the Crown Investigatory Office (Wikipedia).

Civic vs kin.evidence: House Vandimion and her brother Leonardo back her (Wikipedia).

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Aristocratic world; heroine 'punches up' at corrupt elites (AV Club).

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Gods of time and love grant powers; rival holy orders (Wikipedia).

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Scarlet drops her composed facade to fight as she likes (ANN).

folkways.japan: Parodies the Japanese web-novel 'villainess' genre, where a noble daughter's broken engagement and loss of face start the story.

delivery.evidence: ANN: villains are 'smug' caricatures and slavery is 'bad, full stop'; AV Club: nobles are 'human garbage bags', no 'shades of subtlety'.

personified.ideology: the wronged fight back against abusers

delivery.note: Two reviews describe the noble antagonists as cartoonish targets whose role is to be deserving of Scarlet's punches; the message is carried by comedy rather than speeches.

winners_losers: Scarlet and the slaves she frees win; Kyle, Terenezza and the corrupt noble faction are humiliated. Sympathy goes to the abused who strike back.
to_verify: Gender-role themes that IGN France says the manga explores more fully than the anime
Whether the Palmia cult arc portrays organized religion broadly or a single villain cult
Reviews cited are of volume 1 and of the anime; later volumes may vary
